messages:
IncBot: :warning: PAGING — Elevated 5xx and gateway timeout rate on /v1/chat (us-west-2). 10m error pct = 7.1% (alert threshold 4%). Paging: @Maria Chen @Alan SRE @Devin Patel

Maria Chen: oncall ack. Any recent infra changes?

Alan SRE: no deploys. I'm seeing a surge of 502/503 from upstream provider-2 and a concurrent spike in egress latency. Logs:

```
[2026-03-15T12:11:02Z] route=/v1/chat status=502 upstream=provider-2 latency=9.2s err="upstream reset"
[2026-03-15T12:11:03Z] route=/v1/chat status=503 upstream=provider-2 latency=10.8s err="service unavailable"
```

Alan SRE: runtime health looks stable; heap/cpu fine. Seems provider-2 failing on certain batch sizes.

Devin Patel: I'll immediately divert best-effort traffic to local-fallback and reduce provider-2 concurrency. Applying traffic policy now.

```
redwoodctl traffic apply --route=/v1/chat --selector="priority!=high" --to-model=local-fallback --reason="upstream degradation"
redwoodctl provider set provider-2 --max-concurrency=25
```

Devin Patel: canarying change for 3 minutes.

Priya (CS): we've got 2 customers flagged as experiencing timeouts (BetaCo, FinApps). Marking customer-impacting and notifying CS.

Jordan Ops: opening an incident doc and setting status page to "degraded". Linking ticket numbers.

IncBot: Alert storming noted across channels eng-runtime and eng-sre. Consider dedupe rules.

Maria Chen: agree on dedupe. Also this rule pages on percentage alone which triggers on low-volume bursts. Suggest change: require both pct > 4% and absolute 5xx count > 200 over 10m, and add a 'for: 4m' window. That should reduce noise during small bursts.

Alan SRE: draft Prometheus rule update:

```
- alert: High5xxOnChat
  expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",code=~"5..",route="/v1/chat"}[10m]))
         / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",route="/v1/chat"}[10m]))) > 0.04
  unless: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",code=~"5..",route="/v1/chat"}[10m])) < 200
  for: 4m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

Alan SRE: also adding a label match to differentiate upstream-caused errors: `upstream="provider-2"` and a separate alert provider_upstream_issues to drive operator actions not immediate pages.

Devin Patel: created temporary suppression for provider-2 via alertctl so we don't get double-paged while we mitigate: 

```
alertctl suppress create --match-label upstream=provider-2 --duration=20m --reason="provider-2 outage"
```

Priya (CS): provider-2 support pinged us; they reported a regional network blip and are rolling a mitigation. No ETA yet. I linked their incident to our ticket.

Jordan Ops: incident created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-033. Added customer impact section and mitigation steps.

Maria Chen: action items:
- Alan: update alert rule (abs count + 4m), add provider_upstream_issues alert and dashboard panel for upstream error ratio
- Devin: keep routing override + concurrency cap until provider confirms stability; prepare rollback plan
- Priya: notify affected customers and collect any request IDs for repros
- Jordan: own incident comms and postmortem scheduling

Alan SRE: I'll add a Grafana panel for absolute 5xx counts by route and a small upstream latency chart. Will reference these in the alert docs. PR soon.

Devin Patel: routing change reduced error pct to 1.9% after 3m. Mirroring to region now.

Maria Chen: good. Please ensure the suppression has an explicit auto-expire and audit logs so we don't permanently mute.

Alan SRE: suppressions are logged and will appear in observability audit trail. Also adding a rule: if provider_upstream_issues alert fires, do not page SLO-ops team for 15 minutes; instead page provider-liaison.

Priya (CS): provider-2 now says mitigated on their side; they suggest we resume normal routing.

Devin Patel: rolling rollback in canary:

```
redwoodctl traffic apply --route=/v1/chat --selector="priority!=high" --to-model=default --reason="provider-2 mitigation confirmed" --canary=10%
```

Devin Patel: monitoring for 10m.

Jordan Ops: updated status page to "partial recovery" and noted affected customers.

Maria Chen: will convene a short post-incident sync tomorrow with eng-sre, eng-runtime, and CS to adjust alert thresholds and suppression policy. We need to balance between noisy pages and missing real regressions.

Alan SRE: adding runbook steps for provider-related failures: identify upstream label, apply concurrency cap, divert non-critical traffic, create suppression with expiry, notify provider liaison.

Priya (CS): collecting customer logs and will attach to incident. If customers want credits, we'll coordinate after postmortem.

IncBot: Incident state changed: mitigated -> resolved (monitoring).

Maria Chen: marking thread for follow-up: alert rule PR, Grafana panels, postmortem doc. Great teamwork.

Devin Patel: leaving handoff notes in the incident page for next oncall. I'll be available for 20 more mins.

Alan SRE: noted. If anything reappears, page me immediately.
